title: Inferior STEMI - nitrate trap
objectives: ASA 324 mg; O2 only if SpO2 <94%
Recognize inferior STEMI as nitrate caution; IV before any nitro
STEMI Alert + direct transport to UVMMC (PCI)
resources: Monitor w/ 12-lead (or show cards), O2, IV kit, NS 1 L, ASA, NTG, stair chair, stretcher. Scene ~12 min from UVMMC (PCI center).
dispatch: UVM Rescue, respond to 14 Maple Ridge Rd for a 62-year-old male with chest pain. Caller is his wife. Patient is conscious and breathing. Time out 0714.

scene.location: Kitchen of a farmhouse, 2nd-floor bedroom stairs nearby. Cold morning, 22 F. ~12 min from UVMMC.
scene.setup: Pt seated at kitchen table, hand on chest, coffee mug, pill bottles on counter (lisinopril, atorvastatin, metformin).
scene.moulage: Pale face powder, misted water for diaphoresis.
scene.roles: Pt actor; wife (bystander/history); evaluator times flow.

patient.name: Gerald Pratt
patient.on_arrival: Seated, leaning forward, pale and sweaty, speaking full sentences, clutching chest. Looks sick.

SAMPLE: Chest pressure, nausea, sweaty, mild SOB, lightheaded when stood
Lisinopril 20 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, metformin 1000 mg BID. **No ED meds** (ask!). No ASA today
HTN, high cholesterol, T2DM, 30 pack-yr smoker (quit 5 yr). Father MI at 58
Shoveling snow off porch ~0630, pain began ~0635, didn't stop at rest
OPQRST: Nothing helps; not positional or reproducible
Substernal -> L jaw and both arms
Constant, slowly worsening. Never had this before

primary: RR 18, mildly labored, equal rise; lungs clear bilat
Radial pulse slow, regular, weak-ish. Skin pale, cool, diaphoretic. No bleeding
No rash, no edema, no trauma. Keep warm
**HIGH** priority: suspected ACS. Should verbalize early 12-lead + intercept/PCI destination
secondary: Non-tender, no crepitus, equal sounds; not reproducible
Clear all fields (re-check after any fluid)
Pulses equal bilat (radial & femoral). No edema, no calf tenderness
No facial droop, grips equal, speech clear
No tearing pain; no point tenderness

vitals.other: Pale/cool/diaphoretic. Lungs clear. Sinus brady (show 12-lead card)

vitals.trigger: ASA given, IV placed, NO nitro (~T+8)
IF NTG given (any route) - 2 min after
vitals.other: Dizzy, "going to pass out", grey. Lungs clear

vitals.trigger: IF no action within 2 min of Stage C
vitals.other: Grey, eyes closed, responds to voice slowly. Lungs clear

flow.give: Read dispatch. Show crew card. Wife: "He was shoveling and just went white."
Give primary findings and Stage **A** vitals as obtained.

branches.then: allow; debrief (protocol: O2 only <94%, dyspnea, CHF)

expected: Intercept vs. direct decided (don't wait on scene)

flow.give: Show **12-lead card** when acquired. Machine reads: ***ACUTE MI SUSPECTED*** - inferior. SAMPLE/OPQRST as asked.

branches.then: wife: "Is it his heart?" Note time; critical (evaluator discretion)

flow.give: Pt asks: "Can I have a nitro? My buddy takes those." Advance to Stage **B**.

branches.then: Stage **C** at +2 min. No IV first = critical (evaluator discretion)
MD: "Hold nitrates, inferior STEMI. Fluids if hypotensive."

flow.give: Pt: "I'm going to pass out." Give Stage **C**. Lungs clear if asked.
Pt stands to walk? -> dizzy. Stairs to driveway, icy steps.
Stage **E**. Evaluator plays receiving hospital / MD.

branches.then: switch to 3.2A: AED, CPR; pull over for analysis/shock
HR 38, BP 84/50, dizzy. Expect IV, NS 500 mL (3.1A), pads on, MD/intercept; no NTG

expected: STEMI Alert radio report (age, sx onset, 12-lead, tx, ETA)

critical: 12-lead not acquired within 10 min of contact
ASA not given (or given w/o allergy/bleed check)
Not transported directly to UVMMC (PCI) w/ STEMI Alert
differentials: Exertional onset, pressure radiating jaw/arms, diaphoresis, STE II/III/aVF, brady
No tearing/back pain, equal pulses & BP, gradual pressure
No pleuritic pain, no calf findings, SpO2 95%, HR slow
Not positional/pleuritic; regional STE w/ reciprocal changes
Brady is from inferior MI; treat cause
debrief: Why does an inferior STEMI change your nitro decision? (RV preload)
What did the 12-lead computer interp say, and what does an AEMT do with that? (6.2)
When is O2 indicated in ACS?
How did you choose destination & intercept vs. direct?
What would you change about crew roles?

crew_card.dispatch: 14 Maple Ridge Rd. 62 y/o M, chest pain. Conscious, breathing. Caller: wife. 22 F, light snow.
crew_card.on_arrival: Kitchen. Male seated at table, hand on chest, pale and sweaty. Wife at his side.

actor_card.Act: Anxious, uncomfortable, rubs sternum. Sweaty. Talk in full sentences. Refuse to lie flat until dizzy.
actor_card.Pain: Pressure 8/10, into jaw and both arms. Started shoveling, never stopped.
actor_card.Say early: "I think it's just indigestion... but I've never felt like this."
actor_card.Ask at ~T+10: "Can I have a nitro? My buddy takes those."
actor_card.If given nitro: After ~2 min: "I'm going to pass out", get quiet, close eyes. Improve slowly once laid flat + fluids.
actor_card.Do NOT volunteer: Father's MI at 58 or smoking history - only if asked

show_cards.title: 12-LEAD
show_cards.caption: Computer interpretation: Sinus bradycardia 58  ***ACUTE MI SUSPECTED*** Inferior injury pattern.  Simulated tracing - not to scale.
show_cards.cue: Show when acquired (target <= 10 min of contact)

show_cards.title: LUNG SOUNDS
show_cards.body: Clear and equal, all fields, bilaterally.

show_cards.title: PILL BOTTLES ON COUNTER
show_cards.body:
Lisinopril 20 mg
Atorvastatin 40 mg
Metformin 1000 mg
(No nitroglycerin, no ED meds)

show_cards.title: MONITOR - Lead II
show_cards.cue: Only if you inject heart block during transport

moulage_tags.text: Non-tender. Pain NOT reproduced by pressing
Equal pulses and BP both arms

learn_more.focus: why nitroglycerin is risky in inferior STEMI / right ventricular involvement, aspirin timing, and the value of prehospital 12-lead transmission and STEMI alerts
